caption: The video captures a powerful, muddy-brown waterfall cascading continuously over a rugged rocky ledge, framed by dense green foliage on both sides. A white pedestrian bridge spans the top of the cascade, while a slender tree trunk stands firmly at the right edge of the frame. Throughout the excerpt, the thick column of turbid water maintains its overall shape and position as it plunges down the rock face. Bright white foam streaks and rivulets constantly shift and reorganize across the surface of the falls, highlighting the turbulent downward flow. At the base, a plume of white mist and spray swells and recedes, its outline changing from frame to frame. The churning pool at the lower left displays swirling patches of white foam that move and reshape over time. The surrounding bridge, rocks, tree, and vegetation remain fixed in their positions, confirming that the visible motion is entirely contained within the rushing water. This static landscape shot emphasizes the relentless, ongoing force of the muddy cascade as it crashes into the basin below.

not ground truth. Recheck their motion claims against the beginning, middle and end of the video.

replace it with a short keyword prompt, physics explanation, checklist or a generic summary.

Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
